findings.quote: but also within Greece itself, you make yourself answerable
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna marked * after καὶ ἐν τοῖς Ἑλληνικοῖς, before καὶ διδοῖς εὐθύνας. The English reads on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: but also in Greek matters [...] and you give account

units.note: The two bracketed sentences in the Greek (days keep the same length for about forty days, where the number is corrupt: μ#; and the lengths of the days grow quickly around the equinoxes) are omitted from the English. This is an omission, not a mistranslation, so no fix is proposed.

findings.quote: because he indicated the routes for sailing out through the regions of the strait
findings.problem: τὸν προσημαίνοντα τοὺς ἔκπλους is a participle modifying Aeolus: he who gave advance signs of (foretold) the sailings out. The Greek has no causal 'because' and no word for 'routes'.
findings.proposed_fix: who foretold the sailings out in the places along the strait

findings.quote: from feeding on these the hunters called galeotes grow fat—fish which, he says, are also called swordfish or sea-dogs
findings.problem: ἐκ δὲ τῆς θήρας αὐτῶν πιαίνεσθαι τοὺς γαλεώτας, οὓς καὶ ξιφίας λέγεσθαι καὶ κύνας. The galeotes are the fish that fatten from hunting the tuna's predators, not 'hunters' as men. The Greek also says both swordfish and sea-dogs (καὶ … καὶ), not 'or'.
findings.proposed_fix: from hunting these the galeotes grow fat—fish which, he says, are called both swordfish and sea-dogs

units.note: The Greek breaks off in mid-sentence (ἀλλ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ἐν); the English correctly marks this with [...]. The sentence continues in chapter 6 at οἷς ἐκείνους ἐλέγχει καθαρεύων.

findings.quote: With arguments of this kind he refutes those earlier writers while claiming precision.
findings.problem: This is the continuation of the sentence broken off in chapter 5 (ἀλλ᾽ οὐδ᾽ ἐν … οἷς ἐκείνους ἐλέγχει καθαρεύων): Polybius is not free (καθαρεύων) of such popular pronouncements even in the very matters in which he refutes the others. The English drops the negation and reverses the point, making him a careful refuter.
findings.proposed_fix: and not even in the very matters in which he refutes those men is he free of them.

findings.quote: ten thousand two hundred stades and more
findings.problem: μυρίων ἐστὶ καὶ πλειόνων ἢ διακοσίων ἐπὶ τοῖς χιλίοις means 10,000 plus more than 1,200, that is, more than 11,200 stades.
findings.proposed_fix: more than eleven thousand two hundred stades

findings.quote: across the Sardinian Sea one may make a corresponding estimate
findings.problem: κατὰ τὸ Σαρδόνιον δὲ λαμβάνειν συναγωγήν: across the Sardinian Sea the distance admits a contraction (is shorter). 'Corresponding' loses this, and the following ἀλλ᾽ ἔστω καὶ ἐκεῖνο τρισχιλίων ('but let that too be three thousand') is a concession for the sake of argument.
findings.proposed_fix: across the Sardinian Sea the distance is reduced

units.note: In the Greek, [ἐλαττόνων ἢ] before ὀκτακισχιλίων is bracketed by the editor (suspect text). The English 'a little less than eight thousand' is fine and gives the sense.
